meaning: The one family a green build could not report is closed, and the cell's build story is complete. u18i left the lane green at 58 artifacts and named the thing the green did not cover: both of the application's web workers were constructed from a string specifier, which webpack 5 does not recognise as a worker request, so no chunk was emitted, no error was raised, and the workers would have 404'd at runtime. One capability answers it — an analyzer-driven rewrite of the era construction into the URL form, provable from the workspace's own worker declaration — and after it the build emits 62 artifacts including both worker chunks, which the runtime chunk references and the service-worker manifest precaches. Three builds agree file for file except the one clock field. Logical-name parity against the era lane is now stated with every asymmetry named: the workers emit, and they emit under a different logical name than the era lane gave them, for a reason read out of the builder's own webpack.

capabilitiesAdded.family: web worker constructed from a string specifier
capabilitiesAdded.reading: The era's CLI carried a webpack 4 worker plugin that treated `new Worker('./x.worker', {type: 'module'})` as a worker request: it compiled the named module under the workspace's webWorkerTsConfig and emitted it as its own chunk. Webpack 5 dropped the plugin and replaced it with a rule in the module graph that recognises exactly one spelling — `new Worker(new URL('./x.worker', import.meta.url), …)`. A plain string is an ordinary argument to that rule, so nothing is parsed and nothing is emitted, and nothing is reported either: this is the one family in this cell that a green build cannot surface. The successor is not a choice — `new URL(specifier, import.meta.url)` is the only construction webpack 5 resolves, the specifier inside it is the one already written, and the options object is untouched — so what has to be proven is that the construction is a worker request at all. That is three readings, each of the tree rather than of a name: the workspace declares web-worker support and the tsconfig it names is present; the string specifier resolves, from the module that writes it, to a file the tree carries that the worker tsconfig's own `include` patterns reach; and the construction's shape matches — the global `Worker` by binding rather than by spelling, a string-literal first argument, and options already declaring `type: 'module'`, which is what the emitted chunk's format has to be. Everything else is refused by name: a specifier this reader cannot read, a specifier naming no worker source, options with no readable `type` or a `type` other than module, an options literal whose membership is not static, a module whose own root scope binds `Worker`. A construction already in the URL form is passed over in silence, which is what makes a second pass a no-op.
refusesRatherThanGuesses: the workspace declares no web-worker support
the first argument is not a string literal
the specifier resolves to no worker source the worker tsconfig includes
the options declare no readable `type`, or a `type` other than 'module'
the module's root scope binds the name Worker

None of the five carries a `new Worker` construction, so the capability had no business in them and said nothing — not a refusal, an absence.

dist/lz.b385162c14c81c3d.js carries the lz-string implementation and a message handler; the chunk is the worker source compiled, not an empty entry.

The two manifests kept from build-12 and build-13 were compared key by key: `timestamp` — 1786503302879 against 1786503355124, fifty-two seconds apart, which is the wall clock of the two builds — is the only key whose value differs, and the 46-entry hashTable is identical between them, worker chunks included.

logicalNameParity.method: Emitted file names with their content hashes elided — every `.<hex>` segment removed wherever it appears in the name — compared as sets against the era lane's 64-file inventory in u18-era-baseline.json. This is the same elision u18i used and it reproduces u18i's reading of the u18i tree exactly.
logicalNameParity.verdict: The migrated lane is no longer a strict subset, and the four names it now emits that the era lane did not are the four worker artifacts under a different logical name. Both lanes emit both workers; they disagree about what the files are called. Every asymmetry is named below and none of them is a missing artifact.

asymmetries.reading: Differential loading, which the Angular 13 line removed from the browser builder. Their absence is the framework's decision and is expected of any Angular 16 build. Unchanged from u18i.

asymmetries.kind: naming difference, not a missing artifact
asymmetries.reading: Both lanes emit both worker chunks. They are named differently because the two bundlers name a worker chunk from different things. The era's webpack 4 worker plugin named the chunk after the module it compiled, giving lz.worker and reminder.worker. Webpack 5 names it from the construction's own options: node_modules/@angular-devkit/build-angular/node_modules/webpack/lib/dependencies/WorkerPlugin.js, at the block that reads `if (!Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(entryOptions, "name") && options && typeof options.name === "string") entryOptions.name = options.name;`, takes the chunk name straight from the `name` property of the options object. This application's two constructions declare `name: 'lz'` and `name: 'reminder'`, and the builder's Lazy Chunk Files table names the chunks lz and reminder accordingly.
asymmetries.whyNotClosed: Closing it by name would mean editing the application's `name: 'lz'` to `name: 'lz.worker'`. That option is not a filename: it is the worker's own `self.name` at runtime and is observable by the application, so changing it to make an emitted filename match a webpack 4 convention would alter runtime-visible state for a cosmetic parity. It is recorded as a difference rather than answered.

logicalNameParity.countReconciliation: 62 = 58 common + 4 emitted under the modern worker chunk name. 64 = 58 common + 2 differential-loading polyfills + 4 emitted under the era worker chunk name. No artifact the era lane emitted is missing from the migrated lane except the two differential-loading polyfills, and the migrated lane still invents nothing the era lane did not also produce under some name.

The one family a green build could not report — workers that compile, bundle green and 404 — was found by parity rather than by the build, and is closed by a capability rather than by an accommodation.
cellBuildStoryComplete.whatItDoesNotClose: Everything under notEstablished. A complete build story is not a complete migration: nothing here has run the application.

notEstablished: Whether the application runs. The build emits 62 artifacts and nothing here loaded one in a browser.

Whether the two web workers work. This round establishes that they are compiled, emitted, referenced by the runtime chunk and precached by the service-worker manifest. It does not establish that either worker answers a message, because nothing here started one.

Whether the emitted worker chunks behave as the era worker chunks did. Not one byte of the two lanes' worker output was compared, and the era output is a webpack 4 chunk where this is a webpack 5 chunk.
Whether the 19 accommodations u18h recorded are behaviour-preserving beyond what each entry claims. This round changed none of them and re-measured none of them.
Whether removing NgxElectronModule leaves the desktop lane working. Still not built here and still not measured.
Whether the emitted bundles behave as the era bundles did. Logical-name parity is a comparison of names.

Whether the worker chunk naming difference has any consequence beyond the filename. The application reads no chunk filename that this round found, but nothing here searched the tree exhaustively for one, and the service worker's manifest is generated from the emitted names rather than from a written-down list.
Whether any other application in this corpus carries the same worker family. The capability is written to the shape rather than to this tree, and it has been run against exactly one tree.
